title: Limited Linguistic Diversity in Embodied AI Datasets

bias_targets.methodology: Quantifying instruction language in Vision-Language-Action datasets across dimensions of lexical variety, semantic similarity (using text embeddings, BERTScore, and PCA), and structural diversity (analyzing part-of-speech patterns, dependency trees, negations, and conditionals) to identify biases toward repetitive, templated, and overly simplified commands.

Qualitatively reviewing datasets for the presence of diverse, multicultural terminology (e.g., non-Western cooking utensils and ingredients) to identify and discuss the tendency of data collection to reflect primarily Western, white audiences.
Evaluating verb and direct object co-occurrence frequencies to identify biases toward a narrow range of interactions and object affordances, which can amplify neural networks' simplicity biases.
